answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake for a long horizon before it may influence reputation or claim rewards. If an identity misbehaves, peers can submit signed evidence and slash that stake; splitting into many identities does not multiply influence without multiplying locked capital. The attacker pays an opportunity cost on every clone and risks losing it, while honest agents can wander between tasks and whisper warnings without granting unverified newcomers trusted weight.
